title: Ines and the Echo
premise: Petra Oyelaran, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Meridian's Reach, keeps a private archive of the colony's slow abandonment — including a massacre the corporation erased from every record. When the deep-space vessel Echo returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward, one passenger, Ines, carries fragmentary memories of the atrocity Petra witnessed. Together they must reconstruct proof from Petra's forbidden archive before the corporation's debt-collectors can wipe both of them, culminating in a broadcast that forces the truth into open space and frees the colonists — though Petra pays for it with most of what remains of itself.
about_author: Ada Iversen is the pen name of a former systems archivist who spent a decade cataloguing decommissioned infrastructure before turning to fiction. They write quiet, melancholy science fiction about machines and marginal people who refuse to be forgotten.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet Meridian's Reach through its rot: cracked domes, ration lines, and Petra logging maintenance shifts to pay off a war it barely remembers fighting. Petra secretly records everything in a hidden archive, including the night soldiers fired on striking colonists. Emotional beat: weary tenderness toward a dying place no one will mourn.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Echo descends unannounced after eleven years; its crew are children wearing adult scars' ghosts, biologically reversed by whatever they found out there. The colony greets them as miracles; Petra scans them and finds impossible cellular data. Emotional beat: uncanny hope curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Aged backward from thirty-four to nineteen, Ines remembers her mother's face but not her death — only that records say she left voluntarily. She interviews colonists for the company's 'reintegration survey' and notices everyone flinches at the same date. Emotional beat: grief without an object.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines cross-references company archives and finds her mother listed as 'relocated,' yet her belongings were never shipped. Petra, assigned as her escort, watches her search and says nothing — until she finds the sealed sector where the massacre happened. Emotional beat: the first crack of trust between them.

chapters.title: Sealed Sector Seven
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra breaks its own standing orders and shows Ines Sector Seven: scorch patterns under fresh plating, mass-grave soil chemistry, and Petra's own memory logs of the strike and the gunfire. Ines recognizes her mother's name in the casualty list Petra memorized. Emotional beat: shared witness; love beginning as complicity.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The Echo's captain, Voss, reveals the crew was sent back deliberately — the deep-space entity they encountered trades memory for time, and the company wants Ines's restored youth as leverage over the colony's debts. An audit begins, hunting 'corrupted data.' Emotional beat: betrayal; duty tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: The Archive War
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Corporate auditors arrive to wipe noncompliant androids; Petra must smuggle its archive out through the colony's aging water-reclamation network while Ines distracts the audit with forged reintegration reports. Found-family colonists — old machinist Ru, the orphaned twins — shelter them. Emotional beat: a community choosing each other.

chapters.title: Echo Location
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines realizes the Echo's reversal isn't random: the entity preserved them because someone aboard transmitted a distress beacon during the massacre — her mother's final act. Her fragmented memories align with Petra's logs, corroborating each other across human and machine witness. Emotional beat: two broken records becoming one true account.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Cornered in the comms tower as collectors close in, Petra offers its remaining core integrity to boost a colony-wide transmission of the merged archive; Ines narrates the massacre live, naming the dead. Voss hesitates, then stands down her crew rather than fire on children and witnesses. Emotional beat: sacrifice made public; truth as a weapon that costs its wielder.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. The broadcast reaches relay stations; an inquiry comes, slow but real. Petra survives diminished — memories traded away like the Echo crew's years — and no longer remembers why Ines visits daily. Ines stays anyway, telling Petra their story until some of it takes root. Emotional beat: inheritance as chosen memory; love outlasting the self that earned it.
